title: A Frog Tries to Eat This Grub. The Grub Eats the Frog Instead

scenes.text: A frog lunges at a grub. The grub wins, almost every time.
The Epomis beetle larva doesn't hide from frogs. It waves its antennae and jaws to call them over.
A frog's tongue fires in a tenth of a second. The grub is faster: it dodges and hooks its jaws onto the frog's face.
Then it hangs on and drains the frog, which is many times its size.
In almost 400 face-offs in the lab, the frogs got a grub into their mouths just seven times.
One toad swallowed a grub whole. Two hours later it threw it back up. The grub then ate the toad.

description:
A frog lunges at a beetle grub, and the grub eats the frog instead.
The larva of the Epomis ground beetle lures frogs and toads by waving its antennae and jaws, dodges the tongue strike, then clamps double-hooked jaws onto the amphibian and drains it. In almost 400 staged encounters at Tel Aviv University, amphibians managed to get a larva into their mouths only seven times. One toad swallowed a larva, regurgitated it two hours later, and was then killed and eaten by it (PLoS ONE, 2011).
Which animal pulls off the biggest role reversal in nature?
subject: Epomis beetle larva
first_comment: The adult beetle hunts frogs too: it climbs onto the frog's back and bites until the frog is paralysed. Which animal would you never expect to lose to its own food?
